topic: The utilisation bound test and response-time analysis
title: Is this task set schedulable? Rate monotonic by hand
instructions:
## A pump controller with three periodic tasks

A water-pumping station controller runs three periodic tasks, each with its deadline equal to its period:

| Task | Worst-case execution C (ms) | Period P (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| T1 sensor read | 1 | 4 |
| T2 control law | 2 | 6 |
| T3 log to flash | 1 | 8 |

Under **rate-monotonic** priority, the shortest period gets the highest priority: T1 > T2 > T3.

## Do this

1. Total utilisation U = Σ C/P.
2. The Liu and Layland bound for n tasks is n(2^(1/n) − 1). Compute it for n = 3. The plot shows the bound as n grows.
3. Response-time analysis: R = C + Σ over higher-priority tasks of ⌈R/P⌉·C, iterated until it stops changing. Compute R for T2 and for T3.
4. The hyperperiod is the least common multiple of the periods: after it, the schedule repeats.
hints: For T3 start from R = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, then recompute 1 + ⌈4/4⌉·1 + ⌈4/6⌉·2.
realityNote: U is below the bound, so the test alone proves the set schedulable; response-time analysis is exact and also shows how much slack each task has. Flight controllers, ABS brakes and pacemakers are certified with this same analysis.
